title: All 129 Passengers Accounted For After Tanker Hits New Orleans River Cruise Boat
excerpt: The Atlantic Asphalt lost control and struck the docked American Heritage at about 12:30 p.m. on Friday. Thirty-two people were hospitalised, none critically, and the NTSB is sending investigators.
body:
• A Marshall Islands-flagged tanker, Atlantic Asphalt, lost control and struck the docked river cruise boat American Heritage at the Port of New Orleans at about 12:30 p.m. local time on Friday, November 13, partially submerging it.
  • All 129 passengers were accounted for. Mayor Helena Moreno said 32 people were taken to local hospitals and none had critical injuries.
  • The Mississippi River was closed to vessel traffic at the scene, and the National Transportation Safety Board is sending a go team to investigate; the cause has not been established.

An asphalt tanker that lost control on the Mississippi River struck a docked river cruise boat in New Orleans on Friday afternoon, rolling the smaller vessel onto its side and sending passengers into the water. All 129 passengers aboard the American Heritage were accounted for by Friday evening, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference, and 32 people were taken to local hospitals with injuries she described as non-critical.

The Port of New Orleans said the 160-metre (520-foot) Atlantic Asphalt collided with the American Heritage at about 12:30 p.m. local time. The paddlewheel cruise boat had docked about two hours earlier and passengers were disembarking when the tanker hit, according to Al Jazeera and the Associated Press. Moreno said the tanker "lost control and collided into the cruise ship," and that the cruise boat began to sink before it toppled over.

The rescue

More than a dozen people in life jackets were pulled from the river, where the water temperature was 19 degrees Celsius (66 degrees Fahrenheit), onto nearby vessels, while other passengers waited near the railing as the boat listed further. Port police, the fire department, the Coast Guard and emergency medical crews responded; the New Orleans Fire Department said 23 units and 57 personnel were sent to the port, according to USA Today. A triage area was set up inside the port administration building, and passengers were taken there for evaluation and assistance.

"Surreal, that's what that was."

— Jamie Holford, witness, to local television

American Cruise Lines, which operates the American Heritage, said guests and crew had been evacuated and that it was deeply concerned for everyone involved. Including crew, at least 180 people were aboard, Moreno said. Two of those hospitalised were police officers who had been helping with the evacuation, according to the Wall Street Journal's reporting from the scene.

The vessels

The American Heritage is a five-deck paddlewheel riverboat built in 2015 with capacity for 150 passengers. It was finishing an eight-day cruise to destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi when it docked in New Orleans. The Atlantic Asphalt, flying the flag of the Marshall Islands, specialises in carrying asphalt and bitumen. Whether it was carrying cargo at the time of the collision has not been established.

What happens next

The river was closed to vessel traffic around the scene on Friday. The National Transportation Safety Board is launching a go team to investigate the collision, USA Today reported. Officials have not said what caused the tanker to lose control, and no reopening time for that stretch of the river had been announced as of Friday evening.
nri_angle: Mississippi river cruises from New Orleans are a popular US holiday route for Indian-American families; all passengers are safe, but the river closure and NTSB inquiry will shape sailings from the port in the coming days.
author: Diaspora Desk
